Lowering the groundwater level by pumping from wells or
dewatering of excavations or tunnels will cause an
increase [n the effective stress in the subsoil affected,
which can lead to excessive settlement of adjacent
structures. Also, if pumps do not have an adequate
filter, the leaching of fines from the subsotl can easily
result in excessive settlement of structures at
considerable distance from the pump.

In areas where natural underground cavities can occur,
e.g. karst features in the Yuen Long basin, increase in
effective stress or downward ravelling of soil due to
heavy pumping may lead to subsidence or the formation
of sinkholes (Siu & Wong, 1984).

8.3.3 Procedure

in the tnvestigation of the safety of existing features or works, the first
requirement is an appreciation of the changes to the ground that are likely to
occur. The ground Investigation will need to provide knowledge of the
subsurface materials, together with the examination and testing of samples to
assess the effect that the changed conditions are Itkely to have on these
materifals. If some cases, it may be necessary to carry out a detailed analysis
to estimate the effect of the changed conditions on the safety of the existing

features and works.
